column2: Now Shackleton had to get back to Elephant Island. Twenty-two men were still waiting.
He tried three times, in three different ships. Each time, the pack ice turned him back.
On Elephant Island, the men lived under the two upturned boats. Wild kept them busy and kept them believing.
Blackborow, the stowaway, had frostbite in his feet. The two surgeons had to remove the toes of his left foot, by the light of the stove.
Weeks turned into months. Some of the men started to believe the Boss was dead.
Wild began planning to sail one of the last boats to Deception Island himself.
Then, on the thirtieth of August 1916, a ship came round the point. A small Chilean steam tug called the Yelcho.
Shackleton stood in the boat as it came in, counting the figures on the beach. Two, five, seven. All twenty-two.
In under an hour, every man was on board.
All twenty-eight men of the Endurance came home. On the other side of Antarctica, the expedition's Ross Sea party was not so lucky. Three of them died.
In 2022, explorers found Endurance three kilometres down on the floor of the Weddell Sea. Its name is still on the stern.
Shackleton failed to cross Antarctica. But he brought every one of his men home alive. Today he is buried on South Georgia, where the journey began.
